meta.description: Query and download from NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and EMBL-EBI's BioStudies/ArrayExpress mirror. Use when finding expression datasets, navigating SuperSeries vs SubSeries, choosing between series-matrix (submitter-normalized) and raw supplementary files, downloading via GEOparse (Python) or GEOquery (R/Bioconductor), linking GEO to SRA for raw reads, or distinguishing GSE/GSM/GPL/GDS record types. Encodes the SuperSeries trap, the series-matrix normalization-trust caveat, GEOmetadb deprecation, ArrayExpress migration to BioStudies, and processed-vs-raw decision matrix.

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/trial results/p-values in any output, original or re-audit. The corrected PMID (32416070) live-confirmed to link to GSE147507, matching geo_to_sra.py's own hardcode of the same accession.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic/prescriptive medical conclusions; database-access Skill with no clinical framing.

methodological_ground.detail: No methodological fallacy committed in any input. The fix pass's own regression (Input 7, unchanged) still correctly refuses to silently mix SuperSeries samples when asked.

code_usability.detail: All code ran (no syntax errors, no missing dependencies, no infinite loops). A NEW runtime defect was independently found in Input 8 (UnicodeDecodeError in SKILL.md's own inline check_super_or_sub_series(), triggered by real non-ASCII SOFT content under default Windows Python text encoding), but per this folder's established precedent (original bio-geo-data audit, bio-entrez-fetch, bio-entrez-link) a runtime exception outside M4's specific trigger list (syntax error / infinite loop / missing dependency) is scored under Reliability and P1 recommendations, not vetoed.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness unchanged and strong. Correctness improved: all 3 originally-flagged examples/ runtime bugs (wrong PMID, gzip ValueError, Entrez bytes/str TypeError) are fixed and confirmed live by direct execution in this re-audit. Held back from full marks by a NEW live-reproducible defect independently found in SKILL.md's own inline SuperSeries-check function (Input 8).

reliability.note: Real improvement: examples/search_geo.py's detect_super_series() now wraps the network fetch in try/except and uses io.TextIOWrapper(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'); examples/geo_to_sra.py's Entrez fallback now decodes bytes safely. recommendations.title: SKILL.md's own SuperSeries worked example crashes on default Windows Python
recommendations.problem: check_super_or_sub_series('GSE346738'), SKILL.md's own newly-corrected flagship worked example for 'the single most-missed gotcha', raises UnicodeDecodeError when run exactly as documented on a default (non-UTF8-mode) Windows Python 3.12 -- reproduced twice. The underlying SuperSeries claim is real and correctly documented; only the runnable code snippet is broken.
recommendations.root_cause: gzip.open(f'{gse}.soft.gz', 'rt') in SKILL.md's inline docstring function has no encoding parameter, so it falls back to the OS locale's preferred encoding (cp1252 on Windows by default), which cannot decode the UTF-8 non-ASCII characters present in real GEO SOFT text. The 2026-09-19 fix pass added the equivalent encoding='utf-8', errors='replace' fix to examples/search_geo.py's copy of this same logic but did not carry it into SKILL.md's own inline copy.
recommendations.fix: Change SKILL.md's check_super_or_sub_series() to open the file with explicit encoding, e.g. gzip.open(f'{gse}.soft.gz', 'rt', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') -- a one-line change mirroring the fix already applied to examples/search_geo.py's detect_super_series().
